# NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-NVFP4
## Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 4B | | **Architecture** | Looped (latent-recurrent) normalized-GPT with interleaved sliding-window attention (SWA) and full-attention layers | | **Precision** | NVFP4 | | **Context Length** | Up to 256K tokens | | **Supported Languages** | English | | **Best For** | General-purpose reasoning on a small footprint | | **License** | [OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenMDW/OpenMDW/refs/heads/main/1.1/LICENSE.OpenMDW-1.1) | | **Release Date** | October 16, 2026 | **NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-NVFP4** is a looped (latent-recurrent) large language model (LLM) trained by NVIDIA. The model employs a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved hybrid sliding window attention (SWA) and full attention layers. By repeatedly applying a shared block of layers, Dory1.0-4B can spend more compute per token allowing it to scale intelligence. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use.

Dory (Looped LM) Architecture: The layer stack is divided into three groups: Input (I), Recurrent (R) and Output (O). The shared Recurrent block (R) is applied multiple times between the Input and Output blocks, and the input is reinjected into every loop. In Dory, the Input and Output blocks have 8 layers each, while the Recurrent block has 20 layers.
## Highlights * **Elastic Inference Compute:** A single checkpoint serves different inference compute budgets. By changing how many times the shared block of layers is applied, you can trade inference compute for accuracy to suit each task, with no retraining and no model swap. * **Token Efficiency:** With looping, the model needs fewer generated tokens to solve a task. Extra computation per token goes into thinking in latent space rather than into longer outputs. * **Memory-Efficient Looping:** Standard looping shares parameters across loops but still stores a separate KV cache for each one, so memory grows with every added loop. Dory supports last-loop KV caching, which keeps a single cache per recurrent attention layer. When enabled, Dory carries no KV-cache overhead relative to an equivalent non-looped model, regardless of the inference loop count. * **Native NVFP4 Pre-training:** Built on a normalized-GPT (nGPT) backbone, Dory is pre-trained natively in NVFP4, NVIDIA's 4-bit floating-point format, before continuing in BF16. * **Multiple Formats:** The model is available in BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4 and Q5_K_M formats. ## License/Terms of Use **Governing Download Terms:** Use of this model is governed by the [OpenMDW-1.1 model license](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/). ## Benchmarks

(1) AA-LCR: We use the corrected answer keys (from AA-LCR v1.1) but keep the older judge (Qwen3-235B-A22B) instead of GPT-5.6 Luna.
(2) GDPval-AA v2: Elo ratings of selected reference models (out of 12): DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1223), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (992), Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (925), gpt-oss-120b (745).
(3) Repeats: Number of repeated runs per benchmark: AA-Briefcase-Lite (1), GDPval-AA v2 (1), AutomationBench-AA (1), Terminal-Bench 4.0 (1), SciCode (8), Humanity's Last Exam (1), GDP.pdf text-only (5), AA-Omniscience (10), AA-LCR (16).

Looping is token-efficient. As the loop count increases, the model solves the same tasks with fewer generated tokens.
## **Quick Start Guide** ### **vLLM** **Note:** Dory support in vLLM is under review in [vllm-project/vllm#60149](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60149). Until it is included in a vLLM release, install vLLM from that PR: ```shell VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install "git+https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git@refs/pull/60149/head" ``` `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` reuses compatible prebuilt vLLM kernels, avoiding local CUDA compilation. This section will be updated once a vLLM release supports Dory. #### **Launch the Server** ```shell vllm serve --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-NVFP4 \ --hf-overrides '{"n_recurrent_loops": 2, "recurrent_kv_cache_mode": "per_loop"}' \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 1
